Patrick — thank you for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. We opened a priority bridge at 09:18 PST (bridge id INF-4132). Initial triage shows an increased kernel-level OOM on a subset of our hosted inference pool which increased request retries and occasionally surfaced 502/504 to downstream callers. At first glance dedicated pools for Lumen Health do not appear to be impacted, but we are validating.

Immediate actions we have taken:
- Opened a dedicated bridge and escalation channel (INF-4132).
- Pinpointed a serving host group with high mem-pressure; isolating and gracefully draining nodes.
- Rolled a temporary routing rule to avoid the affected host group for Lumen Health traffic.
- Capturing KV-cache and prefix metrics, saving relevant logs and a sample token stream.

Next steps (owner):
- Marcus Lin: full heap / kernel log collection + traces (ETA 30m).
- Naomi Feldman: coordinate a short exec note for Lumen leadership (ETA 45m).
- Ben Carter: check quota/rate rules to confirm no burst misrouting (ETA 20m).
- Soojin Lee: validate Dedicated pool isolation (ETA 25m).

We will provide a customer-facing summary for your CTO in the next update. Attaching a short logs bundle and an initial postmortem skeleton as soon as it is available.

Thanks — Dylan

Subject: RE: Incident report incoming — Lumen Health production impact

Bridge INF-4132 update — quick technical summary:
- Root cause (prelim): a regression in memory accounting introduced in deployment INF-runtime-v2.8.3 that underestimates ephemeral KV cache memory when sequence-length spikes occur. At ~08:48 PST we saw a coordinated workload (large batch of long-context requests) which pushed several hosts over the kernel threshold and triggered OOM handling.
- Scope: affecting a subset of hosted inference hosts running the v2.8.3 runtime. We have isolated ~18 hosts and are draining them.
- Impact: intermittent 502/504 and elevated tail latency for ~12% of Lumen Health tokens in the window 08:48–09:22 PST. Dedicated nodes for Lumen (customer-dedicated-07) show no memory pressure and no errors on their metrics.

Mitigation performed:
- Rolled back the v2.8.3 runtime on the impacted autoscale group to v2.8.2 (completed 09:40 PST).
- Added a temporary KV-cache soft-limit for long-sequence requests to prevent immediate re-trigger.
- Restarted drain/replace of affected hosts with v2.8.2.

Short-term risk: if we resume normal traffic patterns before the full replace completes, we may see brief retries; putting a short-term traffic cap on hosted pools for high-sequence requests until replace is finished.

I am attaching kernel logs and GC traces to the bridge notes. Will follow with an incident timeline and a postmortem draft.

Marcus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
